Determinism between standard libraries, after the audit: visibility orders copies of one vertex (the convex pieces of a collider share it) by vision_extends and is_on_a_bound, not by the STL's choice - an explosion at a wall gave other triangles on Windows and Linux; its operator< compares the angle only, the order of ties decided in one place (sort_near_equal_runs). Bullet obstacles at equal distance ordered by the whole entity id (two entity types can share a pool index). libstdc++ client vs libc++ server, 240 s of bots: 0 desyncs.

Server browser: servers on the local network keep the key their signed answer proved - a LAN tournament is one row with its matches and Results, LAN rows can be starred and are joined by the key (a password saved for it is found again); a reinstalled LAN server takes its new key at once. Favorites are matched to LAN rows as to the list's: one row, the star lit, the name given by hand. A tournament's match keeps its own name ("[alice] vs [bob]") over a favorite's. A favorite whose ping got no answer is asked again every second for 5 s before it goes. A hand-added favorite with another key listed at its address shows it: "Another server (another key) is at this address now." / "Reinstalled? Add it again with its new key." The favorites filter finds a map's name too. Results set off from its trophy.

Network after the audits: a heartbeat request is padded to 1200 bytes (an answer only ~2x it, nothing for a spoofed flood), so many may ask - 64 addresses from the internet (at most 32 per IP), 256 from the local network. A signed ping answer's signature is checked only for an answer to what was asked (a flood of others cost an Ed25519 verify each on the game thread); the server's public key passed in instead of derived per answer. Browser players refused by the signalling see why (the socket's close no longer overwrites it); a relayed message never refuses. The "channel closed" notes matter only in their tick - cleared every pass (a note could drop a new browser player who got the same WebRTC id), notify_game cut. The masterserver never bans an empty name (a trailing space in the banlist took every casual server off the list).

Tests and skills after the audits: the build lock counts a ninja unless the game (a debugger, valgrind) runs under it; slot_reuse fails unknown cases; the browser screenshot script cleans up (full path, Xvfb timeout, every port); the soak counts its 8 runs; rsync instead of cp + rm; xvfb-run -d.
